title: Does a fundamental-matrix gate on the matches, fitted from the matches alone, let bundle adjustment survive mismatches?
lede: an epipolar gate removes 93% of 10% random-pixel mismatches (5% of good observations lost) and takes 5% contamination from 0.168 to 0.0061 object radii, but a RANSAC start does as well at 10% and better at 20%; near-miss mismatches are mild for a robust loss already. Synthetic only
summary: Follows sensing-baoutlier with the geometric verification it left out. For each pair of nearby views a fundamental matrix is fitted by RANSAC from the matches alone (normalised 8-point, Sampson distance under 2 px, no use of the wrong poses) and an observation is kept if half its pairs accept it. On the 12-view rig it removes 94%, 93% and 89% of random-pixel mismatches at 5%, 10% and 20% while losing 2%, 5% and 16% of good observations; at 5% Cauchy adjustment improves from 0.168 to 0.0061 object radii (floor 0.0015). It is no better than the RANSAC pair start: equal at 10% (0.045) and worse at 20% (0.41 to 0.77 against 0.13). Near-miss (10 to 40 px) and along-epipolar-line mismatches are removed at 79–87% and are mild for a robust loss anyway (0.005 at 10%). Limits: synthetic, my own mismatch models, 6 seeds, untuned gate settings, scoring set differs from sensing-baoutlier.
